newsitem.title: UK: IPAI to drop Chinese data from its regular reports.
newsitem.headline: IPAI to drop Chinese data from its regular reports.

text.p: The International Primary Aluminium Institute (IPAI) is to drop after only two months inclusion Chinese production data from its regular monthly reports, starting with March data, which will be released next Monday.
The IPAI added Chinese data to its long-established series in February this year, incorporating data for January.

But many analysts said new and untried data from this source and the break in the continuity of previous well-established aggregations had caused difficulties in tracking world production trends, it added.
In a release the IPAI said that the strength of consumer resistance to the additional information has been such that it has decided, at least for the present, to withdraw the addition.
"The March primary aluminium report will not therefore include China in Area 4/5 (Asia)...Data from China will be excluded from all other regular reports until further notice," the IPAI said.
However, other additions made from January 1 of Tadjikistan, Kazakhstan for alumina and Montenegro will still be included.

"The IPAI intends to pursue its constructive dialogue with the CNNC (Chinese National Non-ferrous Metals Industry Corporation) in order to determine the best way forward for reconciling the Institute's objective of achieving full coverage of world primary aluminium production in the best interests of users of IPAI statistical series, which remain at the core of all the Institute's activities," it added.
